summary: mymatasan now has an audit trail, and all three apps share one implementation. Deleting a recording, purging a camera's footage, changing retention, and viewing or downloading a segment now each record who did it, from where, with what client, and — for a deletion — which camera and time range were lost, captured before the row is removed. Previously mymatasan recorded none of this: it was the only app in the suite with no audit log, and the one holding the actual video. "Who watched this footage" is a mandatory line item in GDPR Article 30 records and in essentially every government CCTV tender, and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact. Camera credential changes (username only, never the password) and user create/update/delete are recorded too. New admin-only routes GET /api/audit and GET /api/audit.csv expose the trail for review and export; there is deliberately no delete or update route, because a trail the recorded party can edit is not a trail. Under this, the audit implementation moved to domain/shared/audit: myidsan and myseliasan had each written their own and the two had already drifted (only one truncated hostile input, only one had retention, only one recorded the user agent), and adding a third copy would have made that worse. myseliasan gains retention, input truncation, the user-agent field, and filtering by outcome, actor and date range; its fleet-health report now applies the date window in the query rather than filtering the newest 500 rows afterwards, which previously let a busy period outside the window push in-window entries off the end of the report.
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive. mymatasan gains the audit_log table (created by the auto-migrator, no migration) and two new admin-only read routes. myseliasan's existing audit_log gains an additive user_agent column and an actor index, also auto-migrated; its GET /api/audit accepts new optional filters and its existing ones are unchanged. myidsan is unchanged in behaviour and keeps its existing metric names. No config changes. The trail's read UI is not built yet — the routes and the page grant exist, but no screen renders them.
